Custom firmware for the [OpenTrickler RP2040 Controller](https://github.com/eamars/OpenTrickler-RP2040-Controller),
forked from eamars' v1.14 and developed against a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W with an
A&D FX-120i scale.

**This is a personal fork.** It has been developed and tested on one machine
with one powder. It dispenses gunpowder charges for ammunition reloading -
verify charge weights independently, exactly as you would with any dispenser.

## Which file do I want?

| File | Board | |
|---|---|---|
| `opentrickler-v2.0-pico2_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico **2** W (RP2350) | developed and tested on this |
| `opentrickler-v2.0-pico_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico W (RP2040) | **builds, but untested** |

The Pico W build had never linked before this release - the OTA path called a
bootrom function that only exists on RP2350. That is fixed, but no RP2040
hardware was available to run it on, and RAM sits at 88% there. If OTA misbehaves
on a Pico W, BOOTSEL and a drag-and-drop always recovers it.

Hold **BOOTSEL** while plugging the board in, then drag the `.uf2` onto the
`RPI-RP2` drive that appears.

## Read this before you flash

**Your settings will reset.** Charge-mode settings and Learn Powder settings
return to defaults on first boot (EEPROM revisions 12 and 4). Profiles are
kept. Write down anything you have hand-tuned first.

**Re-run Learn Powder afterwards.** Existing profiles keep whatever coarse stop
threshold is already baked into them, so none of the fit changes below take
effect until you do.

## Measured on the development machine

26.5 gr charge, +/-0.06 gr bracket, one powder, one machine - your numbers will
differ, but this is what the changes below were validated against:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Throws inside bracket | 7/20 | **13/13** |
| Mean error | +0.074 gr | **-0.015 gr** |
| Spread (sd) | 0.047 gr | **0.023 gr** |
| Throw time | 8.3 s | 10.0 s |
| Coarse handoff | 5.3 gr | **2.0 gr** |

## What this fork adds over upstream

- **Learn Powder** - an auto-tune wizard that characterises a powder on both
  tubes (flow per rps, scale lag, dead time), fits a profile, and runs
  confirmation throws against it
- **Per-throw adaptive tuning** - bounded feedback that adjusts the profile as
  you charge, assigning blame to the bulk or fine tube from where the throw
  actually went wrong
- **Phase-split lag compensation** - coarse and fine measure consistently
  different lag, so each gets its own value instead of one blended figure
- **Session statistics and CSV export** from the web portal, plus a raw export
  of every Learn Powder calibration throw
- **Acceptance brackets** with selectable Normal and Match tolerances
- **WiFi OTA updates** and a mobile-friendly portal layout
- Auto-tune indicator on the 12864 display when lag compensation and Learn are
  both active

## Fixed in this release

**Charge accuracy**

- **Auto-lag was eating its own correction.** With lag compensation on, the fine
  motor is stopped early by design, so what auto-lag measured afterwards was the
  residual *after* compensation worked - not transport lag. It learned that
  smaller number, compensated less, overshot, and measured smaller still. On the
  development machine it walked the fine lag from a fitted 0.70 s to 0.49 s,
  putting +0.056 gr into every charge. Now disabled whenever lag compensation is
  on, and off by default.
- **The fine landing margin was a 1-sigma budget** while the coarse handoff uses
  3 sigma, letting the fine tube land about three times too fast - roughly a
  third of throws fell outside the bracket by arithmetic alone. Now a settable
  **Landing Sigma**, default 2.
- **Deterministic overcharge.** Live tuning could ratchet the coarse handoff
  narrower indefinitely on clean throws with no reference to measured variance.
  Tightening is now floored by the coarse tube's own measured spread.
- **Pooled-variance bug.** Lag spread was computed across coarse and fine throws
  together. They have different means, so pooling inflated the apparent spread
  by the gap between them - about 9x on measured data - and that inflated number
  was setting the coarse handoff.

**Learning and fit**

- **Live tuning could never actually tighten the handoff** - its floor was the
  exact value the Learn fit handed it, so the narrowing branch was a no-op.
- **A stale tuning baseline fought every new fit.** Bounds were anchored to
  whatever was loaded at power-on and never refreshed, so the first adjustment
  after a Learn run dragged the profile back toward the values it had just
  replaced.
- **Throw time was predicted at roughly half of actual.** The fine taper was
  modelled as a linear ramp, but the controller drives it proportional to
  remaining error, which is an exponential approach; measured dead time was not
  counted at all. A throw predicted at 5.8 s that really took 11.8 s now
  predicts 11.5 s.
- Per-throw tuning is suppressed during Learn's confirmation throws, so the pass
  rate describes the profile being measured.
- The fit no longer extrapolates coarse speed beyond what the calibration ladder
  actually measured.

**Learn Powder cup handling**

- **The cup-return step could hang waiting for a manual zero.** It tested for
  the cup against a fixed threshold, but the scale is re-zeroed after every
  throw with the powder still in the cup - so an empty cup returned after
  dumping 130 gr reads about -130, not 0. Detection is now relative to the empty
  pan. The tare that follows also waits for the scale to settle first, since the
  A&D discards commands it receives while unstable.

**Other**

- `Ver:`/`VCS:` on the version screen no longer show blank on builds without a
  reachable tag.
- Lag settings moved from Session & Bracket to the Charge Mode page.

## Tuning it

Three settings control the trade between speed and margin:

- **Time Goal** (Learn Powder) - the fit spends every second under this buying a
  closer bulk handoff, so a lower goal gives a faster throw and a wider handoff.
- **Bulk Safety Factor** (Learn Powder) - how many times the coarse tube's own
  measured 3-sigma stop scatter the handoff must cover.
- **Landing Sigma** (Learn Powder) - how many sigma of fine landing error must
  fit inside the bracket, which is what caps the landing speed. Landing error
  scales directly with landing speed, so going from 1 to 2 halves the spread and
  costs roughly a second and a half per throw.

Raise Bulk Safety Factor or Landing Sigma if you see overthrows.
